heroHeadline: Cairo Widens Its Mediation Role: Sisi Hosts CIA Chief on Iran, Greece-Cyprus Defense Ministers, and Iraq's Hakim in a Single Week
heroSubtitle: President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi held an unannounced meeting with CIA Director John Ratcliffe in Cairo on September 20, 2026, pledging 'full support for efforts aimed at reaching a comprehensive agreement that resolves the Iranian crisis' amid Egypt's mediation between Washington, Tehran and Arab states. On September 19, Sisi directed the government to expand data centers, 5G and AI investment, targeting $12 billion in digital outsourcing exports by 2029. On September 21, Water Minister Hani Sewilam told a Cairo briefing that all options remain on the table to protect Egypt's Nile water rights, calling Ethiopia's operation of the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam illegitimate. On September 22, Egypt hosted the sixth Greece-Cyprus-Egypt trilateral defense ministers' meeting, agreeing to jointly protect East Mediterranean energy infrastructure. On September 23, PM Madbouly told the UN General Assembly that the two-state solution faces 'unprecedented challenges' and pressed for Security Council reform, while meeting Bulgaria's president on trade. On September 24, Sisi received Iraq's Hikma Movement leader Ammar al-Hakim in Cairo. Separately, Suez Canal Authority data showed August 2026 revenue up 56.7% year-on-year to $567.1 million as Red Sea shipping traffic continued recovering, though still trailing pre-2023 levels.
footerNote: Data sourced from Egyptian official records, UNESCO, academic Egyptology research (Shaw, Lehner, Hawass), major international outlets, IMF, Human Rights Watch, and institutional analyses.
